question: What is the Resulticks acquisition supposed to unlock — revenue synergies or cost savings?

beat.line: What matters next is cross-sell traction, and growth outpacing the cost of integration.
beat.headline: CROSS-SELL TRACTION
beat.action: The pile flattens into a calendar page; a paper hand enters and points at it.

sources: What matters next: Evidence that Resulticks' customer base is adopting the broader platform (cross-sell traction), and that revenue growth from the combined entity is accelerating faster than the cost of integration.
Without that, the acquisition becomes a value-destructive financial engineering move rather than a strategic unlock.
prompt:
TESSERA STYLE SHEET
1. Modern editorial paper collage. Bold magazine composition, refined 2D motion design.
2. One dominant flat block-colour background for the whole shot: lime green. Never a rainbow, never a gradient.
3. Subjects are black-and-white halftone photographic cutouts with rough white torn-paper edges: objects, machines, buildings, maps, coins, screens, vehicles, anonymous paper hands. Never a recognisable person's face.
4. Diagram elements are flat matte paper shapes and ribbons in cream, black, pale yellow, or the background's contrasting colour. Real paper texture, print dots, small tape pieces.
5. Consistent upper-left light. Small paper-layer shadows only.
6. Everything is flat matte printed paper. No glow, no neon, no bloom, no halos, no luminous edges. Nothing emits light. Not glossy 3D. Not live action.
7. Headline typography: one extra-bold sans-serif, black or cream, printed on paper chips, large, safe margins. English spelling and letterforms accurate and stable. Only the headline text in the copy list, nothing else.
8. Motion: elements enter fast with slight overshoot and a stable landing, then hold a clear reading window. One strongest visual focus at a time. No camera shake. Movement starts on the first frame; a small loop continues at the end. No empty frames.
9. Numbers, when specified, are printed complete from their first visible frame. Never counting up, never morphing, never redrawn.
10. No brands, logos, watermarks, or text beyond the copy list.
11. 16:9, exactly 5 seconds, one composition, at most one crisp cut.
12. Identity anchor: rough white torn-paper edges on every cutout; small paper shadow from upper-left light.

BEAT
Ground: lime green.
Subjects: the document pile; a paper hand; a calendar page.
Opens on the document pile, carried over from the previous shot, which transforms as the action begins.
Action: The pile flattens into a calendar page; a paper hand enters and points at it.
Ends holding on the pointing hand.
Headline printed on a paper chip: "CROSS-SELL TRACTION".

COPY LIST: "CROSS-SELL TRACTION". Exact strings; nothing else appears in frame.

AUDIO: No voice, no speech, no dialogue, no lyrics. Light paper-slap and tape sound effects only; no music.
expandedPrompt:
integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] Cinematic 2D-animated modern editorial paper collage. The scene opens with a dominant, flat lime green block-color background featuring a matte paper texture. Centered in the frame is a document pile, rendered as black-and-white halftone photographic cutouts with rough white torn-paper edges and small shadows cast to the bottom-right from a consistent upper-left light source. Immediately, the document pile flattens with a fast, snappy motion and a slight overshoot into a single, flat calendar page cutout, also in black-and-white halftone with white torn edges. Simultaneously, a large, extra-bold sans-serif headline "CROSS-SELL TRACTION" appears in black ink, printed on a rectangular cream-colored paper chip with a visible paper grain, positioned in the upper section with generous margins. At 00:02.000, an anonymous paper hand—a black-and-white halftone cutout with rough white torn edges—enters the frame rapidly from the right, pointing its index finger directly at a specific date on the calendar page. The hand lands with a slight bounce and holds its position. The composition remains static for the remainder of the shot, with the paper elements exhibiting a subtle, rhythmic floating loop to maintain a sense of depth. All elements are flat matte printed paper; there are no glows, gradients, or luminous effects.

overall_soundscape: A sharp, tactile paper-slap sound occurs as the document pile flattens into the calendar. This is followed by a quick, sticky sound of adhesive tape being pressed down as the headline chip appears, and a final, crisp paper-click sound as the hand points to the page.
